title: Indians Among 13 Killed as Bus Hits Stopped Truck in Ras Al Khaimah
excerpt: The bus, carrying 41 people, struck a truck that had stopped on Al Watan Road after a mechanical failure. India's consulate in Dubai has contacted bereaved families and opened a 24/7 helpline, 800-46342.
body:
• Thirteen people, including Indian nationals, were killed early on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, when a passenger bus carrying 41 people hit a truck stopped on Al Watan Road in Ras Al Khaimah, the UAE Ministry of Interior said.
  • The death toll rose from 11 to 13 after two injured passengers died in hospital; 14 others were injured.
  • The Consulate General of India in Dubai has contacted bereaved families and opened a 24/7 toll-free helpline, 800-46342, for information and assistance.
  • How many of the dead are Indian nationals has not yet been confirmed; the consulate said further details are being ascertained.

Indian nationals are among 13 people killed in a bus-truck collision in Ras Al Khaimah, the Consulate General of India in Dubai confirmed on Tuesday. The consulate said it had reached out to the bereaved families and was working with local authorities to provide all possible assistance.

"We are deeply saddened by the tragic road accident in Ras Al Khaimah that claimed lives of several people, including Indian nationals. The Consulate has reached out to the bereaved families and is closely working with local authorities to provide all possible assistance and support."

— Consulate General of India, Dubai, on X

What happened

According to the UAE Ministry of Interior, the accident occurred early on Tuesday morning on Al Watan Road in Ras Al Khaimah. A passenger bus carrying 41 people collided with a truck that had stopped along the roadside following a mechanical failure. The collision initially claimed 11 lives; two more victims later died of their injuries in hospital, taking the toll to 13. Another 14 people sustained injuries of varying severity and were taken to nearby hospitals.

Emergency teams, including police, search and rescue units, ambulance services and Civil Defence personnel, responded to the scene. Ras Al Khaimah Police have referred the case to the relevant authorities for further investigation into the circumstances of the collision, and officials have urged the public not to circulate rumours or unverified information about the accident.

Help for families

The consulate said further details were still being ascertained, including how many of those killed or injured are Indian nationals. Families and community members seeking information can call the consulate's 24/7 toll-free helpline: 800-46342.

Second deadly UAE crash in two weeks

The crash comes less than two weeks after a multi-vehicle collision in Fujairah killed 14 people, including four Indian nationals, in an accident involving 23 vehicles that also injured around 30 people. Tuesday's accident is the latest in a series of fatal road incidents in the Emirates involving Indian workers and travellers, a community that forms the largest expatriate group in the UAE.

Indian officials said they would continue coordinating with UAE authorities as identification of the victims proceeds and assistance to the families is arranged.
nri_angle: Indian nationals are among the dead in the UAE's second fatal crash involving Indians in two weeks; the Dubai consulate helpline is the families' first point of contact.
